title: PCAT: Functionality and Data Stealing from Split Learning by Pseudo-Client Attack
motivation: Server has incentive to steal client functionality to avoid revenue sharing in SL; existing attacks fail on unknown/deep client models
problem_framing: How to steal client functionality inputs and labels when client model structure is unknown and complex without being detected
key_insight: A well-trained server model alone can construct a pseudo-client model using very limited data; intermediate server models during training provide extra guidance knowledge
method_signature: Pseudo-Client Attack using server model knowledge transfer without requiring client model structure
evaluation_criteria: Accuracy gap between pseudo-client and victim model; label inference accuracy; input reconstruction quality (SSIM)
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: UnSplit test accuracy drops to 22.1% on CIFAR-10 with VGG16; norm-based label inference only works for imbalanced binary classification
evidence_for_taste: search space could be too large to converge
thinking_moves: Abandon model inversion search paradigm entirely
Recast problem as knowledge transfer from server model
Exploit intermediate training checkpoints as learning targets
Use label alignment to train pseudo-client without client awareness
